newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Danny shuts Mississippi River entrance.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Danny shuts Mississippi River entrance.

text.p: The mouth of the Mississippi River was shut to commercial shipping traffic on Friday as Hurricane Danny swept across coastal Louisiana, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The river's commercial shipping entrance at Southwest Pass remained shut through the day after the slowly moving storm made landfall north of the pass before moving off to the northeast and stalling east of New Orleans.

High winds, steady rain and wind-driven water bombarded Plaquemines Parish southeast of New Orleans Friday afternoon, more than six hours after Hurricane Danny punched into the "toe" of Louisiana's boot-shaped coastline there.
About 100 boats appear to have been damaged or sunk at a large marina in Buras, La., where storm waters rose four to five feet (1.2 to 1.5 metres) within a few minutes earlier in the day.

The crew of the fishing boat Nasty Two was riding out the storm in the captain's house of their partially sunken boat after rescuing two other fisherman from a sinking boat in the Empire deepwater canal. The Nasty Two was tossed onto rocks and itself sank in shallow water, the Coast Guard said.
